Eighteen comments

The Air Tune

This is my version of Liz Carroll’s composition, which is slightly different from the original, I believe. I’m not sure how it should be categorised but I think it’s a slow reel. It’s a fiddle tune but sounds nice on whistle.

I’ve never tried playing this tune in the session, but I might do in the near future. Rakish Paddy is a nice tune to follow it.

↳ Posted by slainte on April 16th, 2004.

I got this from “Her infinite variety - celtic women in music and song” (I think that’s the name of it), a collection of female “celtic” artists. On that CD it’s played by Trian together with two tunes called “The cliff dwellers” and “Cutting the waves”. Not sure if they’re here already, but I’m working on them.

Very nice tune, anyway. And it works great with Rakish Paddy. :)

The Air Tune, X:8

This is basically an accurate ABC rendering of the transcription presented in Liz Carroll’s own book of her collected compositions, published in 2010, except for a minor tweak I’ve made to the format - I haven’t changed anything material, I’ve just added the Last Time bar.

Note there are no “triplets”, the little runs in groups of 3 notes being correctly notated as 2-semiquavers-plus-a-quaver. Where those grouplets are of repeated As (Bars A4 & B4) I would, as a fluter/whistler, play A rolls, but I wanted to preserve the book (fiddle) text rather than substitute dotted crotchets with a roll sign (~A3).

Also note the 1st and 2nd time bars of the two sections - I don’t think any of the other transcriptions posted here have quite got the details of those right (or some other bits….. except perhaps if they’re accurate transcriptions of someone playing it “differently”! :-D ).

Here are the ABC header lines for my transcription which The Session entry format doesn’t accept:
T:The Air Tune
C:Liz Carroll
O:USA
B:Liz Carroll Collected (2010 - ISBN 9780615378145)
Z:Jem Hammond 20:6:19 after David James (transcriber for the book)
R:“Slow Piece”
M:C
L:1/8
K:D

↳ Posted by Jemtheflute on June 20th, 2019.
